beats.care: She is 23, from Kalleda village in Warangal, and was spotted by her school PE teacher in Class 9. Talent gets found when someone looks.
beats.what: Deepthi Jeevanji won the women's 400 metres T20 gold in Aichi-Nagoya in 56.36 seconds, over two seconds ahead of the silver medallist.
beats.why: She won the same event in Hangzhou in 2023 and took bronze at the Paris Paralympics, so she came in as the favourite.

cards.body: Her own old Games record, set in Hangzhou, was 56.69 seconds.
cards.caption: Deepthi's winning time, a new Games record

cards.body: Two Japanese runners, Niina Kanno and Akane Kato, took silver and bronze. Elsewhere, Bhavina Patel won table tennis bronze, and Pramod Bhagat and Manisha Ramdass reached the mixed badminton semi-finals.
She beat her own Games record, but she has run even faster before: her world record is 55.06 seconds.

cards.q: Who should get more prize money?

cards.why: She won this event at the last Asian Para Games and a Paralympic bronze, so she started as the favourite.

hook: From a Warangal village to a *Games record*. How fast did Deepthi run?

learn.t: T20 is the para-athletics class for athletes with an intellectual impairment. Deepthi also holds the 400m T20 world record.

watch: The Asian Para Games end on 24 October. Spill's prediction on whether India reaches 100 medals closes then.
